solution.excerpt:
Credit Card | Order not Converted | Payment Deducted
Generated: 2026-09-02T14:00:00.000Z

Issue:

Order PK260816-61163937_260823115706539 was placed on Aug 23 at approximately 5:31 PM IST using Cybersource credit card payment (pk-CybersourceCcPaymentModeV2). The customer was successfully charged and the payment authorization was confirmed by the Cybersource payment portal (Request ID: 7874865289346261303129). However, the order remained in temporary status and was never converted to a real order. The tokoCleanUpTemporaryOrdersJob subsequently expired the order to TEMPORARY_EXPIRED status. On Aug 31, admin.vamshi.s manually converted the temp order to normal, but it landed at CHECKED_INVALID because critical payment data was never created. The reporter has now requested to cancel the order.

RCA:

The root cause is a missing Cybersource notification callback. After the customer completed the Cybersource payment authorization, Cybersource was supposed to send a server-to-server notification to the Hybris endpoint at /notification/provider/{paymentProvider}/. This notification triggers the payment notification handler strategy, which is responsible for converting the temporary order to a real order by creating the CreditCardPaymentInfo and PaymentTransaction entries.

The notification callback was never received by Hybris. Without it, the notification handler strategy was not invoked, and the temp-to-real order conversion never occurred. The Cybersource saveSubscription() step, which normally creates the CreditCardPaymentInfo during this notification flow, also never ran. As a result, no paymentInfo and no PaymentTransaction entries were created for this order.

Approximately 1 hour and 21 minutes after order creation (6:52 PM IST), the tokoCleanUpTemporaryOrdersJob ran. This job checks for temporary orders that have exceeded their configured temporaryOrderRemovalTimeoutHours threshold. For pk-CybersourceCcPaymentModeV2, this timeout is set to 1 hour. Since no payment notification had been received, the order appeared as an abandoned temporary order and was set to TEMPORARY_EXPIRED.

On Aug 31, admin.vamshi.s performed a manual remediation to convert the TEMPORARY_EXPIRED order to a normal order (CREATED status). However, this manual conversion only changed the order status without creating any of the payment-related artifacts that the normal notification flow would have produced. Specifically, the following are missing from the order: paymentInfo (CreditCardPaymentInfo link), PaymentTransaction entries with paymentProvider set to cybersourceCc, requestToken containing the Cybersource response token, Order.deliveryMode, and Order.paymentStatus. The DefaultCheckOrderService.check() method detected the missing paymentInfo at the null check and set the order to CHECKED_INVALID.

Previous investigation confirmed that the two CreditCardPaymentInfo objects in the customer profile were both created on March 15, 2026 (5 months prior to this August order) and belong to a different completed order. No new paymentInfo was created during the August checkout because the Cybersource notification flow that creates it never executed. This means there is no recoverable payment data on the Hybris side to link the customer's deducted payment to this order.

The failure is on the Cybersource (payment provider) side. The payment was authorized successfully but the notification callback to Hybris was not sent or was not received. This is confirmed by the payment provider themselves, who acknowledged the authorization and instructed the team to proceed with settlement on the Hybris end (Comment 6). However, without the notification having created the necessary payment artifacts, settlement cannot be triggered from Hybris.

Possible remediation:

The reporter has explicitly requested to cancel the order (Comment 10, Sep 1). Given that the order is stuck at CHECKED_INVALID with no recoverable payment data on the Hybris side and no payment transaction entries to link the deducted payment, cancellation is the appropriate remediation path.

1. Cancel the order PK260816-61163937_260823115706539 and move it to CANCELLED status via a HAC Groovy script. This will clear the stuck order from the system.

2. Since the customer's payment was deducted by Cybersource (authorization was successful), a refund must be processed for the customer. The refund should be initiated from the Cybersource payment portal directly, as there are no PaymentTransaction entries on the Hybris side to trigger an automated refund. Alternatively, the payment provider can void the authorization if settlement has not yet occurred.

3. No further Hybris-side remediation (such as creating paymentInfo or payment transactions) is recommended, as the reporter has decided to cancel rather than attempt a full payment data reconstruction. This is the correct decision given the complexity of reconstructing payment artifacts that were never created through the normal flow.

4. Investigate with Cybersource why the notification callback was not sent for this specific transaction. This is a payment-provider-side issue that could affect other orders if it recurs. The temporaryOrderRemovalTimeoutHours of 1 hour for pk-CybersourceCcPaymentModeV2 is relatively tight; if Cybersource notifications can be delayed beyond 1 hour under certain conditions, consider increasing the timeout to provide a larger window for late-arriving notifications.

tickets.summary: Script to set FOC entry price to 0.01 and retrigger consignment process
tickets.description:
For orders mentioned in ticket : SAHME-3403. NERP not accepting 0.00 value from promotion rule discounted FOCs. Script sets totalPrice to 0.01 on FOC order entries and retriggers YS03 consignment business process from sendConsignmentToExternalERP.

It is similar to PC-52664: [Jira Link]

solution.excerpt:
Script to set FOC entry price to 0.01 and retrigger consignment process
Generated: 2026-09-01T20:58:00.000Z

---

Hi Lerato ,

This PC ticket carries the remediation script for the 30 orders listed in SAHME-3403. The accessory consignments on these orders are stuck because NERP is rejecting the zero-price line items sent by Hybris.

Promotion rules on the ZA store set the accessory totalprice to 0.00 (Free of Charge) while the baseprice retains the original value (e.g. 1499.00 or 1295.00). When Hybris sends the consignment feed to NERP, the TokoSDAdditionalDataPopulator.populateGiftWithPurchaseData() method detects the 0.00 totalprice via TokoOrderService.doesConsignmentContainFOCNonPromotion() and classifies the entry as FOC non-promotion. This triggers a DOC_TYPE override from the region's normal sales order type (YS10) to the FOC order type (YS03). NERP then attempts to look up a valid T184 entry for the combination YS03 + the material's Item Category Group + the FOC item category (YNB1), finds no valid mapping, and rejects the consignment with the error "This order type is not accepted (YS03)".

DB verification confirms this across all 30 orders. Each order is split into two consignments: the _1 consignment containing the phone (SM-F*) shipped successfully with a GERP billing number, while the original consignment containing the accessory (EF-* or EB-* or EP-*) is stuck at SHIPPING_REQUESTED (27 orders) or SHIPPING_PREPARATION (1 order) because NERP never created the sales order. The order process is stuck at waitForWarehouseSubprocessEnd waiting for the accessory consignment to complete. All payments are captured successfully.

By setting the accessory entry totalprice from 0.00 to 0.01, the entry will no longer be classified as FOC non-promotion by doesConsignmentContainFOCNonPromotion(). This prevents the DOC_TYPE override, keeping it as YS10 (normal order), and the item category will use the standard mapping. T184 has valid entries for YS10 + the accessory material groups, so NERP will accept the order. The consignment process is then restarted from the sendConsignmentToExternalERP node to re-send the corrected feed to NERP.

This is the same remediation approach confirmed and successfully applied in SAHME-3392 and SAHME-3386 for the ZA region, and in CLME-2989, CLME-2836, and CLME-4092 for the Chile region where the NERP teams approved sending the zero-price SKU value as a nominal amount.

The script is attached to this PC ticket (script-SAHME-3403-foc-price-remediation.groovy). It is idempotent (only modifies entries where totalprice equals zero) and only restarts processes in ERROR or WAITING state. A reusable approved PC ticket exists under PC-52664 (Closed, REUSABLE label) originally created for SAHME-3375 with the same logic.

Rollback: set totalPrice back to 0.00 and nonGiveAwayFOC back to true on the affected order entries.

Thanks,
Aryan.

## Remediation
- Reusable PC ticket: PC-52664 (Closed, REUSABLE, approved by D2C Team)
- Similar PC: PC-52664 (referenced in ticket description)
- Script: script-SAHME-3403-foc-price-remediation.groovy (attached to PC-53378)
- Parent ticket: SAHME-3403 (Blocks relationship, In Progress)
- Logic: Set FOC entry totalprice from 0.00 to 0.01 on YS03 consignments, restart consignment process from sendConsignmentToExternalERP
- Orders: 30 ZA-region orders from SAHME-3403
- Rollback: Set totalPrice back to 0.00 and nonGiveAwayFOC back to true

Request to allocate 0.01 value on accessory SKUs
Generated: 2026-09-01T17:24:31.812Z

---

Hi Lerato ,

I investigated the 30 orders listed in the ticket and confirmed that all accessory consignments are stuck because NERP is rejecting the zero-price line items. Here is what happened.

Promotion rules on the ZA store set the accessory totalprice to 0.00 (Free of Charge) while the baseprice retains the original value (e.g. 1499.00 or 1295.00). When Hybris sends the consignment feed to NERP, the TokoSDAdditionalDataPopulator.populateGiftWithPurchaseData() method detects the 0.00 totalprice via TokoOrderService.doesConsignmentContainFOCNonPromotion() and classifies the entry as FOC non-promotion. DB verification confirms this across all 30 orders. Each order is split into two consignments: the _1 consignment containing the phone (SM-F*) shipped successfully with a GERP billing number, while the original consignment containing the accessory (EF-* or EB-* or EP-*) is stuck at SHIPPING_REQUESTED (27 orders) or SHIPPING_PREPARATION (1 order) because NERP never created the sales order. The order process is stuck at waitForWarehouseSubprocessEnd waiting for the accessory consignment to complete. All payments are captured successfully. Two orders (ZA260806-52232515 and ZA260823-67050593) have already progressed past this stage with their accessory consignments showing COMPLETED status.

By setting the accessory entry totalprice from 0.00 to 0.01, the entry will no longer be classified as FOC non-promotion by doesConsignmentContainFOCNonPromotion(). This prevents the DOC_TYPE override, keeping it as YS10 (normal order), and the item category will use the standard mapping. T184 has valid entries for YS10 + the accessory material groups, so NERP will accept the order.

A reusable approved script exists under PC-52664 (Closed, REUSABLE label) originally created for SAHME-3375. The script sets FOC entry totalprice from 0 to 0.01 on YS03 consignments and restarts the consignment process from the NERP SO creation node. Only the order list needs to be updated to match these 30 orders. The script is idempotent (only modifies entries where totalprice equals zero) and only restarts processes in ERROR or WAITING state.

Kindly confirm if we can proceed with applying the 0.01 price to these 30 accessory entries so we can push the orders forward.

Thanks,
Aryan.

- Script: script-SAHME-3375-foc-price-remediation.groovy
- Adaptation: Copy script to script-SAHME-3403-foc-price-remediation.groovy, replace 3-order list with 30 SAHME-3403 order codes, update header to PC-52664(SAHME-3403)
- Logic: Set FOC entry totalprice from 0.00 to 0.01 on YS03 consignments, restart consignment process from sendConsignmentToExternalERP
